newsitem.title: CROATIA: Tudjman says he making good recovery.
newsitem.headline: Tudjman says he making good recovery.

text.p: Croatian President Franjo Tudjman, reportedly ill with cancer, said on Sunday he would be capable of performing his duties for a long time because he was making a swift recovery.

In a presidential statement carried by Croatian state radio, Tudjman thanked all those who wished him well and said he was "carrying out his official duties normally", dismissing reports that his health had worsened.
"(Tudjman) informs them with pleasure that his recuperation is progressing very well," the statement said.
The 74-year-old president, who steered Croatia to independence from federal Yugoslavia in 1991, is said by U.S. sources to have untreatable stomach cancer.

Recent reports in independent media, quoting Croat medical circles, said Tudjman's condition was worse than believed at first in November, when he returned from medical treatment in the United States.
Diplomats in Croatia said they now believed it was "a matter of months" before he is incapacitated, or possibly dead.
Tudjman's unusual absence from public life last week triggered speculation that he had undergone another bout of medical treatment.
But he appeared in public for the first time in 10 days on Friday and seemed in better health, with rosy cheeks and moving with his old ease, though still much thinner than three months ago.

Croatian presidential elections are due this summer, and analysts believe the ruling Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ), with no obvious candidate to replace Tudjman, would try to avoid them in case he is unable or unwilling to run.

Independent media carried reports in the past few months that the HDZ is planning to change the constitution so that the parliament -- in which they hold the majority till 1999 -- elects the president.
But Tudjman hinted on Sunday he would run in the elections.
"With the people's and God's will, he (Tudjman) will be able to perform his (presidential) duties for a long time," the statement said.
